title: Working Scientifically
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Working Scientifically Worksheets (Fair Tests, Tables and Bar Charts)
standard_text: Ask relevant questions and use different types of scientific enquiries to answer them; set up simple practical enquiries, comparative and fair tests; make systematic and careful observations and, where appropriate, take accurate measurements using standard units, using a range of equipment, including thermometers and data loggers; gather, record, classify and present data in a variety of ways; record findings using simple scientific language, drawings, labelled diagrams, keys, bar charts, and tables; use results to draw simple conclusions, make predictions for new values, suggest improvements and raise further questions.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on working scientifically: asking questions, fair tests, measuring, tables, bar charts, odd results, predictions and conclusions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Change one thing and keep everything else the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

Scientists ask questions and answer them with fair tests and careful measurements.

  • Change one thing, measure one thing, keep everything else the same.
  • Measure with rulers, stopwatches and measuring jugs. Look closely with a magnifying glass.
  • Record results in tables and bar charts, check odd results and say what you found out.
Example

Light and bean plants: change what?

The question names it

Answer: the amount of light

Example

Paperclips held by each magnet: present how?

Comparing amounts

Answer: a bar chart

Common mistakes

  • Changing two things at once.
  • Not checking a result that does not fit.
  • Writing a conclusion that is not based on the results.

faq.a: A test where you change only one thing and keep everything else the same, so you know what caused the result.

faq.q: How should I record my results?
faq.a: In a table as you go, then in a bar chart or labelled diagram if it helps others understand them.

faq.q: What do I do with a result that does not fit?
faq.a: Check it by repeating the test. It might be a measuring mistake.
